dilemma_zone — DRIVE decide op

• Data kinds: any → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.dilemma_zone(v, *, reaction: 'float', decel: 'float', amber: 'float', intersection_width: 'float', car_length: 'float', accel: 'float' = 0.0) -> 'Dict[str, object]' (to call the implementation directly, import drivedecide; drivedecide.dilemma_zone(v, *, reaction: 'float', decel: 'float', amber: 'float', intersection_width: 'float', car_length: 'float', accel: 'float' = 0.0) -> 'Dict[str, object]'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("dilemma_zone"))

Usage

Dilemma zone of the amber (yellow) signal (Gazis, Herman, Maradudin 1960).

The amber light comes on while you are at distance x before the stop line at speed v:

can stop ⇔ x ≥ x_c = v δ + v²/(2a) (δ = reaction, a = decel)

can clear ⇔ x ≤ x_0 = v τ + ½ a₁ (τ − δ)² − (w + L) (τ = amber, a₁ = accel ≥ 0, w = intersection width, L = car length)

(a₁ = 0 is the basic form. Acceleration is taken to run from after the reaction to the end of the amber. If τ ≤ δ, the acceleration term is 0.) max(x_0, 0) < x < x_c is the dilemma zone (cannot stop and cannot clear. x < 0 is excluded because the stop line has already been passed), x_c ≤ x ≤ x_0 is the option zone (both are possible).

Reading of Japanese law: the Rules of the Road (Kyosoku) Appendix Table 1 (amber) says "if close to the stopping position and unable to stop safely, you may proceed" = it is enough to pass the stop line (there is no obligation to clear the intersection while the light is amber). Under that reading, call with intersection_width = car_length = 0 (x_0 = vτ). GHM's "clear the intersection" is a strict reading that assumes there is no all-red time.

Return values: x_stop_min = x_c, x_clear_max = x_0, dilemma ((lo, hi) or None), option (likewise), length (length of the dilemma zone, 0 if none), v_critical (the pair of speeds at which x_c = x_0 when a₁ = 0. If there is no real root it is empty = no dilemma at any speed). v is a single number (for arrays use np.vectorize or similar).
